subject: literature
passage: For a month, Ximena had been teaching her grandfather to send text messages, and for a month he had insisted the phone was a nuisance he would never need. He typed with one finger, sighed at every mistake, and reminded her that a proper letter took real effort. The evening after Ximena moved away to begin her nursing course, her phone buzzed: "Arrived safe? Room cold? I bought you warm socks. Will mail." It had taken him, she guessed, nearly twenty minutes to write. The message most strongly suggests that Ximena's grandfather ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: still believed that a text message could never be sincere.
choices.B: had always enjoyed using the phone and only pretended to dislike it.
choices.C: cared enough about his granddaughter to use a tool he had resisted.
choices.D: wanted Ximena to give up her course and return home.

explanation.why: The grandfather complained about the phone and typed slowly, yet right after Ximena left he spent about twenty minutes writing her a caring text. His concern for her outweighed his dislike of the phone.
explanation.A: Incorrect. He chose a text to express real care, which shows he was willing to use it sincerely.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The slow, effortful message suggests he still found the phone hard; nothing shows he secretly enjoyed it.
explanation.C: Correct. He overcame his resistance to the phone to check on her and tell her about the socks.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The message asks about her room and promises socks; it never asks her to come home.
